S50Z26.five_day_thesis: Five sessions have produced a flat round trip - 1,053.4 on 10-16 to 1,053.7 today, +0.3 points - through a 1,043.1 trough on 10-21, with 1,050 max pain unmoved across all five and 12 sessions in total. The highest-signal event was the dealer-gamma round trip: net board GEX ran +797.9 (10-16) to +174.5 to -1,653.0 to -1,338.4 to -107.8, two sign flips in five sessions, while the ATM-zone sum traced the mirror path +1,575.3 to +1,219.8 to +547.4 to +835.9 to +1,538.4, so the long-gamma shelf that broke on 10-21 is now fully rebuilt. No IV compression accompanied it - 11.60% to 10.73% to 12.17% to 11.61% to 11.72%, net +0.12 - which is why today's 7.78-point 1-sigma day is almost identical to 10-16's 7.69. What did move in one direction is put positioning: pc_oi 0.978 to 1.03 to 1.04 to 1.048 to 1.076, five straight rises on +3,958 total OI (+21.2%), with the heaviest five-session builds at 1,050P (+425), 1,050C (+309), 1,020P (+296) and 960P (+258). OI accumulating, no IV compression, put-side positioning rising into a rally and no near-money wall dominating the 1,040-1,060 shelf keeps the series in Protection rather than Pinning at 67 DTE, with the short-gamma corridor at 1,020 (-1,255.6) and 1,000 (-1,283.0) the unresolved risk below the flip.

strategies.name: Iron condor 980P / 1010P x 1110C / 1140C
strategies.rationale: Both short strikes sit outside the live walls - 1,010 is below the 1,020 near-money put wall (1,111 OI, 241 lots) and 1,110 is above the 1,100 call wall (1,592 OI, +114 today) - so the structure is short the range that the rebuilt +1,538.4 ATM-zone long-gamma shelf is actively dampening, with the implied 1-sigma day only 7.78 points and 1,050 max pain holding 12 sessions.
strategies.defined_risk: Max loss = 30-point wing width minus ~5.35 points net credit at mid (put side 7.55 - 4.15 = 3.40; call side 3.15 - 1.20 = 1.95) = ~24.65 points, and only one side can finish in the money. Short-vol payoff is negative-skew - size small.
strategies.invalidation: A daily close below the 1,040 per-strike gamma flip or above the 1,100 call wall.

strategies.name: Put debit spread 1030 / 1000
strategies.rationale: This is the Protection-zone hedge: the 1,020/1,000 short-gamma corridor (-1,255.6 and -1,283.0, the board's two most negative strikes) sits directly under the 1,040 flip, so a break of the shelf is amplified rather than faded, and the 10.60% IV on the 1,030 put is 1.12 points below the 11.72% ATM - the cheapest point on the put smile from which to own that corridor.
strategies.defined_risk: Max loss = net debit ~6.25 points (12.65 - 6.40 at mid); max payoff 23.75 points at or below 1,000.
strategies.invalidation: A daily close back above 1,060 (+391.5 net GEX) with the 1,040-1,060 shelf intact.

strategies.name: Call debit spread 1060 / 1090
strategies.rationale: Spot reclaimed the 1,050 anchor (+3.7) and the flip is now 13.7 points below, but the long-gamma shelf above the money (+391.5 at 1,060, +281.4 at 1,070) means dealers sell into rallies rather than chase them, and the 1,592-contract 1,100 call wall caps the move 46.3 points out - roughly 0.9 sigma over the 67 days left - so the upside is worth owning only in capped, defined-debit form, short of the wall.
strategies.defined_risk: Max loss = net debit ~10.30 points (17.40 - 7.10 at mid), 34% of the 30-point width; max payoff 19.70 points at or above 1,090.
strategies.invalidation: A daily close below the 1,040 per-strike gamma flip.

S50Z26.prediction: The base case is a 1,040-1,060 range held by the rebuilt long-gamma shelf, with 1,050 max pain the centre of gravity and the implied 1-sigma day only 7.78 points (0.74%); the 1,100 call wall caps the upside 46.3 points away, about 0.9 sigma over the 67 days remaining. A daily close below the 1,040 per-strike flip invalidates that read and opens the short-gamma corridor to 1,020 (-1,255.6) and 1,000 (-1,283.0), where dealer hedging amplifies instead of fades. A close above 1,100 on expanding volume and rising IV would instead be the max-pain failure pattern - real flow beating the option structure - and should not be read as mean-reversion back toward 1,050.
S50Z26.risk_note: Educational analysis only - not trade advice, and no position is implied. SET50 options are cash-settled on the SET50 index with no physical delivery, so the dealer-hedging mechanics behind the 1,050 anchor are structurally weaker than for share-settled single stocks: treat the max-pain pull as a tendency, not a guarantee, and note that 67 DTE makes any true pin premature regardless. Defined-risk is not risk-free - the capped max loss on each structure above is real, and short-vol payoffs are negative-skew (small frequent gains, rare large losses), so survival comes from size rather than accuracy. One data caveat: near-money call IVs print 14.08-16.31% at 1,020-1,050 against 9.37-11.20% on the same-strike puts, a put-call parity gap pointing to wide or stale quotes on the call side, so the -0.85 25-delta skew is read off the more reliable OTM wings rather than the ATM rows.
